english.title: Publish name / address / photograph of sex victim in a newspaper
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) during the lifetime of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) when an allegation had been made that an offence of **(..SPECIFY OFFENCE..) had been committed against

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

and being the

(C)_[proprietor]_
(D)_[editor]_
(E)_[publisher]_

of **(..SPECIFY NEWSPAPER OR PERIODICAL..) published therein

(F)_[the name]_
(G)_[the address]_
(H)_[a still picture]_

of **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), being a matter likely to lead members of the public to identify **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) as the person against whom the offence was alleged to have been committed
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) and 5(1) of the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 1992.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
during lifetime of a person
when an allegation had been made that a sexual offence
had been committed against that person
being the proprietor/editor/publisher of a publication
published name/address/still picture likely to lead members of public
to identify that person as the victim

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Attorney General is required for prosecution.
(ii) See section 2 for the offences to which this Act applies subject to the exceptions in section 4.
(iii) See also offence wording: H4321 - for the offence in relation to other publications.
(iv) See also offence wordings: H4322, H4323 and H4324 - which deal with complainants for sex offences (where someone has been accused).

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
